# Evaluating ∫ exp(x)*cos(x) dx

## Integration by Parts (First Application)

Let me set:
- u = cos(x) → du = -sin(x) dx
- dv = exp(x) dx → v = exp(x)

Using the formula ∫ u dv = uv - ∫ v du:

$$I = \exp(x)*\cos(x) + \int \exp(x)*\sin(x)\, dx$$

## Integration by Parts (Second Application)

Now evaluate ∫ exp(x)*sin(x) dx:
- u = sin(x) → du = cos(x) dx
- dv = exp(x) dx → v = exp(x)

$$\int \exp(x)*\sin(x)\, dx = \exp(x)*\sin(x) - \int \exp(x)*\cos(x)\, dx = \exp(x)*\sin(x) - I$$

## Solving for I

Substituting back:

$$I = \exp(x)*\cos(x) + \exp(x)*\sin(x) - I$$

$$2*I = \exp(x)*\cos(x) + \exp(x)*\sin(x)$$

$$I = \frac{\exp(x)*\cos(x)}{2} + \frac{\exp(x)*\sin(x)}{2} + C$$

## Verification

Differentiating the result:

$$\frac{d}{dx}\left[\frac{\exp(x)*\cos(x)}{2} + \frac{\exp(x)*\sin(x)}{2}\right]$$

$$= \frac{\exp(x)*\cos(x) - \exp(x)*\sin(x)}{2} + \frac{\exp(x)*\sin(x) + \exp(x)*\cos(x)}{2}$$

$$= \frac{2*\exp(x)*\cos(x)}{2} = \exp(x)*\cos(x) \checkmark$$

<answer>exp(x)*cos(x)/2 + exp(x)*sin(x)/2 + C</answer>
